audience_question: Which shuttle option meets the minimum range at the lowest upfront cost?
fit_rationale: Four options are compared on the same criteria, and the question combines a range threshold with an upfront cost. An aligned matrix with options as columns and criteria as rows puts every value in the same position, keeps km and USD-thousands units in the row labels, and adds a range-eligibility row so the 200 km filter is visible. It remains a semantic table, so the values read without JavaScript. Bars would show cost or range but not both thresholds cleanly for mixed units.
tradeoff: The matrix shows all four options, including Cedar, which has the lowest upfront cost (USD 35k) but fails the range minimum. That keeps the disqualification visible, at the cost of a denser slide than a single-answer callout would be. The headline names Alder, but the matrix also shows Alder's annual energy estimate (USD 4.2k) is higher than Birch's (3.9k) and Dogwood's (3.8k).
caveats: All figures are fictional planning estimates in thousands of US dollars from one procurement worksheet; no uncertainty ranges were provided.
Estimated annual energy cost assumes 18,000 km of service per vehicle and excludes maintenance and charging-infrastructure costs.
Upfront cost and annual energy cost are shown separately and are not combined; Alder is the lowest upfront cost only among options meeting the 200 km minimum.
Cedar has the lowest upfront cost of all four options (USD 35k), but its 190 km range is below the 200 km minimum, so it does not qualify.
